sections.kicker: Prepared for Balsa by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your Instagram the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: Balsa claims a new Mexican contemporary. The profile does not yet show what that looks like.
sections.keep: Your phrase about ancestral crafts, reimagined. It gives a reason to pay for craft.

sections.label: Front door
title: Three things people
meet first.
Three things
people meet
first.

pins.what: The headline claim is big and unexplained.
pins.why: Many Mexican design brands say contemporary; nothing here says what Balsa's version is.
pins.how: Show the one thing only Balsa does with these crafts, in words and images.
pins.label: Your bio
pins.cost: Without it, Balsa is priced next to every other craft shop.

pins.what: The makers are promised but never named.
pins.why: Charging more needs the people and places behind the piece to be visible.
pins.how: Name the crafts, the towns and the hands on the profile.
pins.label: Your craft
pins.cost: Buyers pay for an object when they could pay for an origin.

pins.what: The profile sends people to a link list, not to a Balsa page.
pins.why: A higher price needs a place that looks like Balsa, not a generic list of buttons.
pins.how: Give Balsa one owned page that carries the story.
pins.label: Your link
pins.cost: The last thing a buyer sees before paying looks like anyone's.

sections.intro: You asked for a look at Balsa, and you said something is off but you could not name it, and that you want to charge more. I spent time on your Instagram. Three things stood out.

title: We fix this kind of

sections.body: It is 20 minutes with me. We go through this page together, on Balsa's own screens, and you leave knowing what to change first.
sections.note: A few short questions first, then you pick a time. You can also just reply to the email.

reference: Hermès, from leather goods. It names its artisans, and the price reads as the cost of their hands.
